summary: Ahead of the Rugby World Cup semi-final in Paris, the All Blacks played down Rieko Ioane's gestures to Ireland fans and Johnny Sexton after their 28-24 quarter-final win, while coach Ian Foster named his team and said New Zealand never consider themselves favourites. Argentina coach Michael Cheika embraced the underdog role and spoke about inspiring his country through ambition rather than results.
one_line: All Blacks defend Rieko Ioane's gestures to Ireland fans and name their semi-final team, while Michael Cheika embraces Argentina's underdog status.
key_facts: Rieko Ioane cupped his ear at Irish supporters at the Stade de France after the final whistle and made a 'shush gesture' with his finger to his lips, after New Zealand's 28-24 win over Ireland.
Johnny Sexton, Ireland's retiring great, gave Ioane a spray after the match.
Ian Foster defended Ioane, saying "It happens on most sporting parks when tensions are high and a lot at stake."
Captain Sam Cane said it is players' different personalities and emotions running high, and that it is always left out there.
Foster made two changes to the starting side and three in total, recalling Sam Whitelock to partner Scott Barrett in the second-row; Brodie Retallick moves to the bench.
Whitelock's breakdown penalty win after 37 phases denied Ireland a match-winning penalty.
Mark Telea was recalled ahead of Leicester Fainga'anuku, having been axed for the quarter-final after missing a team curfew.
Foster called Telea "our form winger" and said he "has done his time".
The All Blacks are 18-point favourites for the opening semi-final on Saturday (6am AEDT).
Argentina beat the All Blacks last year in Christchurch and recorded a maiden win over them in 2020 in Sydney.
Foster said the All Blacks never consider themselves favourites, recalling their shock 2019 semi-final loss to Eddie Jones' England.
Michael Cheika, whose Wallabies lost the 2015 final, said Argentina want to inspire "not just by our results but by our ambition" and that the semi-final is a rare opportunity with "no regrets".
Cheika said his Los Pumas side were too tight earlier in the tournament but have freed up since reaching the knockout stages.
